USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

An encephalopathy precipitant

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with cirrhosis taking lactulose develops recurrent confusion, melena and tachycardia. The family asks whether simply doubling the laxative will address the deterioration. Which additional action is most important?

  1. Stop evaluation once a prior encephalopathy diagnosis is found
  2. Assume melena is a harmless expected lactulose effect
  3. Replace lactulose with an antidiarrheal to retain ammonia in stool
  4. Use the ammonia concentration to exclude active hemorrhage
  5. Evaluate and treat gastrointestinal bleeding
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Evaluate and treat gastrointestinal bleeding

Blood in the gut and hemodynamic consequences can precipitate encephalopathy; symptomatic therapy alone is insufficient.

Understanding the options

Evaluate and treat gastrointestinal bleeding
Blood in the gut and hemodynamic consequences can precipitate encephalopathy; symptomatic therapy alone is insufficient.
Stop evaluation once a prior encephalopathy diagnosis is found
A prior diagnosis does not explain the new bleeding.
Assume melena is a harmless expected lactulose effect
Melena is not a routine fermentation-related adverse effect.
Replace lactulose with an antidiarrheal to retain ammonia in stool
Slowing clearance does not address the precipitant.
Use the ammonia concentration to exclude active hemorrhage
Ammonia cannot exclude gastrointestinal bleeding.
